title: Turing's 1950 paper on computing machinery and intelligence
summary: The Mind paper replaces 'can machines think?' with an imitation game.
body: A. M. Turing, "Computing Machinery and Intelligence" (Mind, 1950), proposes the imitation game as a way of discussing machine intelligence. The v1 article's split into narrow AI (what exists), general AI (not demonstrated), and superintelligence (a speculation) is a later taxonomy. Turing's paper is the 1950 document. It is not a product review of any current system. Selmer Bringsjord and Naveen Sundar Govindarajulu's SEP entry treats the field's goals as philosophically disputed, including whether person-level intelligence is attainable.
